assessments.reasoning: The publisher's Lua 5.4 manual at the registered URL returned the exact digest. Its Introduction calls Lua an embeddable scripting language and separately names the lower-case lua distribution program as the host that uses the Lua library to offer a standalone interpreter. Its account of embedding makes that separation explicit.

challenge.method: Compare the roles of language, library, standalone host, and arbitrary embedding program within the Introduction. Test whether standalone use creates a separate language boundary.
challenge.results: The manual treats embedding and standalone interpretation as two uses of the same language. The lower-case host is identified in the distribution and is not the subject of the index identity.

limitations: The candidate scopes the identity to Lua. Active is the index classification and describes no host or release support.
